application: DVB-T digital terrestrial television (TNT) — 6 national multiplexes (R1-R6) using DVB-T MPEG-4; R9 multiplex launched 2024 in DVB-T2 HEVC. Channels 21-48 (8 MHz each). Migration to DVB-T2 for all multiplexes planned.
typical_devices: Thomson THT740 DVB-T2 receiver, Engel RT7130T2 DVB-T2 set-top box, Samsung/LG/Sony integrated DVB-T2 tuners
power_limit: Varies by site; high-power transmitters up to 20 kW ERP, medium-power 2 kW ERP, low-power gap-fillers 250 W ERP (per GE06 coordination)
regulatory_ref: ANFR frequency plan; Arcom (ex-CSA) multiplex licences; EU Decision 2017/899 (UHF band until 2030); ITU GE06 Agreement
notes: France operates 6 DVB-T multiplexes (R1-R6) plus DVB-T2 R9. The 700 MHz band (694-790 MHz) was cleared in 2019 for mobile/5G. The 470-694 MHz band is reserved for broadcasting until at least 2030. DVB-T2 transition is underway but slower than Italy/Germany.

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors in TV white spaces (interleaved spectrum not used by DTT at a given location)
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital AD4D (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Sennheiser EW-DX (Band Q1-9: 470.2-550 MHz; R1-9: 520-607.8 MHz; S1-10: 606.2-693.8 MHz), Sennheiser EW-D (Band Q1-6: 470.2-526 MHz; R1-6: 520-576 MHz), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (Band DG1: 470-700 MHz)
modulation: Digital proprietary (Shure: Shure Quadversity; Sennheiser: digital UHF wideband)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP maximum (per ERC/REC 25-10 and French national regulations ARCEP)
regulatory_ref: ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422; ECC/DEC/(15)01; French national allocation via ARCEP/ANFR
notes: PMSE operates on a secondary/non-interference basis in TV white spaces. Users must avoid occupied DTT channels at their location. No individual licence required for power up to 50 mW ERP in most EU countries. Frequencies available depend on local DTT channel assignments.

application: Audio PMSE (wireless microphones) in the 700 MHz lower guard band (694-703 MHz duplex gap below MFCN uplink)
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX (S7-10 band: 662-693.8 MHz extends into this region), Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning range)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: ECC/DEC/(15)01; EU Implementing Decision 2016/687; ARCEP Decision No. 2014-1263
notes: The 694-703 MHz guard band sits between the DTT allocation (below 694 MHz) and the 700 MHz MFCN uplink (703-733 MHz). Made available for PMSE on a national basis in France. France allocated 694-703 MHz for audio PMSE use. [FACTCHECK CORRECTION: ECC/DEC/(15)01 specifies the PMSE guard band as 694-703 MHz (9 MHz wide), not 694-700 MHz.]

application: ATSC 1.0 / ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV) digital terrestrial television — UHF channels 14-36 (6 MHz each). Channel 14 = 470-476 MHz through Channel 36 = 602-608 MHz.
typical_devices: SiliconDust HDHomeRun ATSC 3.0 tuner, LG/Samsung/Sony TVs with ATSC 3.0 tuner, Channel Master DVR+, Antennas Direct ClearStream antennas
modulation: ATSC 1.0: 8-VSB; ATSC 3.0: COFDM with LDPC/BCH FEC, up to 4096QAM (1024QAM typical)
power_limit: Up to 1000 kW ERP (maximum for full-power UHF stations per FCC Part 73); low-power TV (LPTV) up to 15 kW ERP
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 73 (broadcast); FCC 47 CFR 2.106 (allocation table); ATSC A/321 (ATSC 3.0 physical layer)
notes: Post-incentive auction (2017), US TV broadcast is confined to channels 14-36 (470-608 MHz). Channel 37 (608-614 MHz) is excluded — reserved for radio astronomy and WMTS. ATSC 3.0 deployment is voluntary and ongoing; many stations simulcast ATSC 1.0 and 3.0.

application: Licensed (FCC Part 74) and unlicensed (Part 15) wireless microphones in TV white spaces, channels 14-36 excluding locally occupied channels
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital AD4D (Band G50: 470-534 MHz; G56: 470-636 MHz; H50: 534-598 MHz; J50: 572-636 MHz), Sennheiser EW-DX (Q1-9: 470.2-550 MHz), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (DF1: 470-608 MHz + 657-663 MHz)
power_limit: Part 74 licensed: 250 mW conducted power (UHF TV band); Part 15 unlicensed: 50 mW (lower limit). Part 74 users may register in white spaces database for interference protection.
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 74 Subpart H; FCC 47 CFR Part 15.236; FCC 24-22 (2024 wireless microphone order); White Spaces Database (WSDB) per Part 15 Subpart H
notes: Licensed users (broadcasters, venues) operate under Part 74 with 250 mW conducted power in UHF. Unlicensed users limited to 50 mW. Both must avoid locally used TV channels. White spaces database registration provides interference protection from TV Band Devices (TVBD).

application: Wireless patient monitoring telemetry in healthcare facilities — co-primary with Radio Astronomy. TV Channel 37, never assigned to any TV station. Four WMTS channels of 1.5 MHz bandwidth each.
typical_devices: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Telemetry T14 transmitter with ApexPro CH system (608-614 MHz and 1395-1400 MHz), Philips IntelliVue Telemetry (primarily 1.4 GHz but also supports 608-614 MHz), Spacelabs Xhibit Telemetry
modulation: Broadband spread spectrum (various); manufacturer-proprietary digital modulation
power_limit: FCC Part 95 Subpart H limits; low power (healthcare facility only, no specific wattage ceiling in Part 95 but devices are designed for in-building coverage typically <100 mW)
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 95 Subpart H (sections 95.2301-95.2395); FCC Report and Order ET Docket 99-255 (June 2000); Radio Astronomy co-primary per 47 CFR 2.106
notes: THIS IS A US-ONLY ALLOCATION. In Europe, 608-614 MHz is simply UHF TV channel 38 (EU numbering). WMTS does not exist as a service category in European regulations. The band is co-primary with Radio Astronomy — WMTS users must coordinate with radio astronomy observatories (especially near Green Bank, WV and Socorro, NM). Must register with a white spaces database administrator for interference protection.
verification_status: CONFIRMED — FCC Part 95 Subpart H (47 CFR §95.1101-1129)

application: Radio astronomy observations — Channel 37 reserved for radio astronomy since 1963 (FCC Docket 15022). Important continuum observation band between 410 MHz and 1.4 GHz allocations.
typical_devices: Radio telescope receivers at NRAO Green Bank (WV), VLA (NM), university radio observatories
power_limit: N/A (receive only — protection from interference)
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR 2.106; ITU-R RA.769; FCC Report and Order 39 FCC 844 (1963); FCC Order 53 FCC 2d 627 (1975, permanent reservation)
notes: Channel 37 has been permanently reserved for radio astronomy since 1975. No TV broadcasting has ever been licensed on this channel. Co-primary with WMTS under carefully coordinated conditions.
verification_status: CONFIRMED — FCC Part 95 Subpart H (47 CFR §95.1101-1129)

application: Guard band separating Channel 37 (WMTS/Radio Astronomy) from the 600 MHz mobile service downlink. Available for unlicensed wireless microphones and white space devices.
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital (J50 band: 572-636 MHz covers this range), Sennheiser EW-DX (R1-9: 520-607.8 MHz does not reach here; S1-10: 606.2-693.8 MHz covers it), unlicensed Part 15 TV band devices
power_limit: Licensed Part 74 wireless microphones: 250 mW conducted; unlicensed operations limited per Part 15
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 27 (600 MHz band plan); FCC 47 CFR Part 15; FCC Incentive Auction Report and Order (FCC 14-50); FCC 24-22 (2024 wireless mic order)
notes: The 614-617 MHz guard band was established after the 2017 incentive auction. No Part 27 licensed mobile operations are permitted here. The FCC allows unlicensed wireless microphone operations and other Part 15 devices in this 3 MHz guard band.

application: Band 71 / n71 downlink — 7 paired 5 MHz blocks (A-G). T-Mobile holds licenses for most of the 600 MHz band nationwide. Used for LTE (Band 71) and 5G NR (Band n71) downlink to mobile devices.
typical_devices: T-Mobile 5G smartphones (Samsung Galaxy S-series, Apple iPhone 12+, Google Pixel 5+), T-Mobile 5G Home Internet gateway (Arcadyan KVD21), Nokia/Ericsson macro cell radios
modulation: LTE: OFDMA downlink (up to 256QAM); 5G NR: OFDMA (up to 256QAM), FDD mode
power_limit: Base station: per FCC Part 27 rules; mobile devices: typically 200 mW (23 dBm) max UE transmit power (uplink band)
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 27; 3GPP TS 36.101 (Band 71 LTE); 3GPP TS 38.101-1 (Band n71 NR); FCC Auction 1002 (600 MHz Forward Auction, 2017)
notes: T-Mobile is the dominant licensee of Band 71 spectrum across the United States. The 600 MHz band provides excellent coverage (low frequency penetrates buildings well and travels far). T-Mobile deployed LTE Band 71 starting late 2017 and 5G NR Band n71 starting late 2019.

application: 11 MHz duplex gap separating 600 MHz downlink (617-652 MHz) from uplink (663-698 MHz). Available for wireless microphones (licensed Part 74 and unlicensed Part 15).
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital (K51 band: 606-670 MHz covers this range), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (DF1: 657-663 MHz portion), Sennheiser EW-DX (S1-10: 606.2-693.8 MHz covers this range)
power_limit: Part 74 licensed wireless microphones: 20 mW EIRP; Part 15 unlicensed: lower limits apply
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 27.5 (600 MHz band plan); FCC 47 CFR Part 74; FCC 24-22 (2024 wireless mic order); FCC 14-50 (Incentive Auction R&O)
notes: The 652-663 MHz duplex gap is NOT licensed for Part 27 mobile operations. The FCC permits wireless microphone use here with power limits lower than in the TV bands. The 20 mW EIRP limit in the duplex gap is significantly lower than the 250 mW in TV bands.

application: Band 71 / n71 uplink — 7 paired 5 MHz blocks (A-G). Mobile device transmit to base station. T-Mobile primary licensee.
typical_devices: T-Mobile 5G smartphones (Samsung Galaxy S-series, Apple iPhone 12+, Google Pixel 5+), T-Mobile 5G Home Internet gateway
modulation: LTE: SC-FDMA uplink (up to 64QAM); 5G NR: DFT-s-OFDM or CP-OFDM uplink (up to 256QAM), FDD mode
power_limit: Mobile device (UE): 23 dBm (200 mW) max transmit power per 3GPP
regulatory_ref: FCC 47 CFR Part 27; 3GPP TS 36.101 (Band 71); 3GPP TS 38.101-1 (Band n71); FCC Auction 1002
notes: Uplink portion of the 600 MHz FDD band. T-Mobile typically deploys 5+5 MHz or 10+10 MHz channel configurations depending on market. Some blocks remain held by smaller licensees in certain geographic areas.

application: Freeview DVB-T and DVB-T2 digital terrestrial television — channels 21-48 (8 MHz each). 6 multiplexes: PSB1 (BBC), PSB2 (D3&4), PSB3 (BBC HD DVB-T2), COM4, COM5, COM6 (all DVB-T), plus local TV multiplex. Freeview HD uses DVB-T2.
typical_devices: Freeview Play set-top boxes (Humax Aura, Manhattan T3-R), Samsung/LG/Sony TVs with Freeview built-in, portable DVB-T/T2 USB tuners
modulation: DVB-T: COFDM 64QAM; DVB-T2: COFDM 256QAM (for HD/Freeview HD multiplexes)
power_limit: High-power transmitters up to 200 kW ERP (e.g., Crystal Palace); medium-power relay transmitters 2-10 kW ERP; low-power gap-fillers 50-250 W ERP
regulatory_ref: Ofcom UKFAT (UK Frequency Allocation Table); Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006; ITU GE06 Agreement; EU Decision 2017/899 (applied via retained EU law post-Brexit)
notes: The UK cleared the 700 MHz band (channels 49-60) in 2020 for 5G. Freeview now operates exclusively in channels 21-48 (470-694 MHz). The UK left the EU but Ofcom maintains compatible spectrum policy. Ofcom published a 2025 study on post-2034 UHF band future.

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors in TV white spaces (interleaved spectrum)
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital AD4D (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Sennheiser EW-DX (Q1-9: 470.2-550 MHz; R1-9: 520-607.8 MHz; S1-10: 606.2-693.8 MHz), Sennheiser EW-D (Q1-6: 470.2-526 MHz; R1-6: 520-576 MHz; R4-9: 552-607.8 MHz), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (DG1: 470-700 MHz)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP (per Ofcom IR 2030 and ERC/REC 25-10); shared/licensed PMSE may get higher limits under Ofcom PMSE licence from Arqiva
regulatory_ref: Ofcom IR 2030 (UK Interface Requirement); ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422; Ofcom PMSE licensing (managed by Arqiva on behalf of Ofcom)
notes: UK PMSE users can operate licence-exempt at up to 50 mW ERP in available TV white space channels, or obtain a shared PMSE licence from Arqiva for specific events/venues. The 700 MHz clearance reduced available PMSE spectrum. Ofcom's PMSE framework is one of the most developed in Europe.

application: Audio PMSE (wireless microphones) in the 694-703 MHz lower guard band. Ofcom allocated this band specifically for PMSE to compensate for spectrum lost in the 700 MHz clearance.
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX (S7-10: 662-693.8 MHz extends close), Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning ranges)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: Ofcom Statement: 'Spectrum for audio PMSE — Use of the 694 to 703 MHz band' (2018); ECC/DEC/(15)01; EU Decision 2016/687
notes: Ofcom confirmed availability of 694-703 MHz for audio PMSE in its 2018 statement. This is a dedicated PMSE allocation, not secondary to broadcasting. Provides 9 MHz of spectrum as partial replacement for PMSE capacity lost when channels 49-60 were cleared.

application: DVB-T2 HD (freenet TV operated by Media Broadcast, plus ARD/ZDF public multiplexes) — channels 21-48 (8 MHz each). Germany completed DVB-T to DVB-T2 HD transition in 2019. All DTT is now DVB-T2 with HEVC (H.265) encoding.
typical_devices: freenet TV CI+ module, Samsung/LG/Panasonic TVs with DVB-T2 HD / freenet TV built-in, Xoro HRT 8730 DVB-T2 receiver
modulation: COFDM DVB-T2: 256QAM, 32k extended FFT, HEVC (H.265) video codec
power_limit: High-power transmitters up to 50 kW ERP (e.g., Berlin Alexanderplatz); medium-power 1-10 kW ERP; low-power gap-fillers
regulatory_ref: BNetzA (Bundesnetzagentur) Frequenzplan; ITU GE06 Agreement; EU Decision 2017/899; Telekommunikationsgesetz (TKG)
notes: Germany fully migrated to DVB-T2 HD by March 2019. The commercial freenet TV service (Media Broadcast) requires a CI+ module or compatible receiver for encrypted private channels. ARD/ZDF public channels are free-to-air in DVB-T2. The 470-694 MHz band is reserved for broadcasting and PMSE until 2030.

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors in TV white spaces
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX (Q1-9: 470.2-550 MHz; R1-9: 520-607.8 MHz; S1-10: 606.2-693.8 MHz), Shure Axient Digital (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Beyerdynamic TG 1000 (470-789 MHz tuning range)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP (per BNetzA Allgemeinzuteilung Vfg. 91/2015 and ERC/REC 25-10)
regulatory_ref: BNetzA Allgemeinzuteilung Vfg. 91/2015; ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422
notes: Germany issues general authorisation (Allgemeinzuteilung) for PMSE in TV white spaces at up to 50 mW ERP. Sennheiser (headquartered in Germany) and Beyerdynamic are major local manufacturers. Professional events may obtain individual frequency assignments from BNetzA for higher power.

application: Audio PMSE (wireless microphones) in the 694-703 MHz lower guard band
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX, Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning ranges)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: BNetzA Frequenzplan; ECC/DEC/(15)01; EU Decision 2016/687
notes: Germany allocated the 694-703 MHz guard band for PMSE use following the 700 MHz clearance. BNetzA confirmed allocation for event technology and broadcasting production.

application: DTMB (Digital Terrestrial Multimedia Broadcast, GB 20600-2006) — digital terrestrial television in UHF band. 8 MHz channel bandwidth. Supports SD, HD, and mobile multimedia services simultaneously.
typical_devices: Hisense/TCL/Skyworth TVs with built-in DTMB tuner, various DTMB set-top boxes (domestic Chinese manufacturers), Rohde & Schwarz DTMB transmitters
modulation: TDS-OFDM (Time Domain Synchronous OFDM); single carrier or 3780 multicarrier; 4QAM/16QAM/64QAM constellation options; LDPC FEC
power_limit: Varies by transmitter class; high-power stations up to 10-50 kW ERP; MIIT sets site-specific limits
regulatory_ref: MIIT (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology) frequency allocation table; GB 20600-2006 (DTMB standard); SARFT/NRTA broadcasting regulations
notes: China uses its own DTMB standard (not DVB-T/T2 or ATSC). The 700 MHz band (694-790 MHz) was released for 5G in 2020, assigned to China Broadcasting Network (CBN). China's DTMB standard has also been adopted in several countries in Southeast Asia, Africa, and Latin America. The 470-694 MHz range continues for DTT.

application: Wireless microphones in TV white spaces — less formally regulated than Europe/US; major events use professional equipment in UHF band
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital (various bands), Sennheiser EW-DX (various bands), domestic Chinese wireless mic brands (Takstar, BBS, Boya)
power_limit: MIIT regulations; generally low power (<50 mW) for unlicensed use; event-specific permits for higher power
regulatory_ref: MIIT Radio Regulations; SRRC (State Radio Regulation of China) type approval requirements
notes: China regulates wireless microphones through MIIT/SRRC. Equipment requires SRRC type approval (radio certification). The regulatory framework for PMSE is less detailed than in Europe or the US. Professional use at major venues/events typically requires coordination with local radio administration.

application: DVB-T2 digital terrestrial television — two federal free-to-air multiplexes: RTRS-1 (first multiplex, 10 channels including Channel One, Russia-1, NTV) and RTRS-2 (second multiplex, 10 channels including REN TV, STS, Domashny). Operated by RTRS (Russian Television and Radio Broadcasting Network). Russia completed DVB-T2 transition and analogue switch-off in 2019.
typical_devices: BBK/Cadena/Selenga DVB-T2 set-top boxes, Samsung/LG TVs with DVB-T2 tuner, Russian-market IPTV/DVB-T2 hybrid receivers
modulation: COFDM DVB-T2: 64QAM or 256QAM, MPEG-4 AVC (H.264) video codec
power_limit: Varies by transmitter; high-power stations up to 5-20 kW ERP; extensive relay network with low-power transmitters (10 W - 1 kW)
regulatory_ref: ГКРЧ (State Commission for Radio Frequencies) decisions; Russian frequency allocation table; Federal Law on Communications (No. 126-FZ); RTRS frequency-territorial plan
notes: Russia operates two federal DVB-T2 multiplexes (RTRS-1 and RTRS-2) that are free-to-air nationwide. Coverage reached 98.6% of population by 2024. A third multiplex exists in Moscow (TVK 34/578 MHz). Russia uses the 470-862 MHz range per ITU allocation but the 700 MHz band status differs from EU — no 700 MHz clearance for 5G has occurred as of 2025. Specific channel assignments vary by region (e.g., Moscow: RTRS-1 on ch.24/498 MHz, RTRS-2 on ch.30/546 MHz).

application: Wireless microphones in TV white spaces — regulated under Russian radio frequency laws
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital, Sennheiser EW-DX, domestic brands; equipment requires Russian type approval (Declaration of Conformity)
power_limit: Low power (<50 mW); specific limits set by Russian national regulations and ГКРЧ decisions
regulatory_ref: ГКРЧ decisions; Russian Federal Communications Agency (Roskomnadzor) regulations; ERC/REC 25-10 (Russia is CEPT member)
notes: Russia is a CEPT member and follows ERC/REC 25-10 framework for PMSE. However, national implementation may differ. Equipment requires Russian type approval. Professional event users often coordinate directly with territorial radio frequency authorities.

application: DVB-T2 broadcasting continues above 694 MHz in Russia. Unlike the EU, Russia has NOT cleared the 700 MHz band for mobile/5G as of 2025.
typical_devices: Same as 470-694 MHz DTT devices
power_limit: Same as main DTT allocation
regulatory_ref: ГКРЧ frequency allocation; ITU GE06 Agreement
notes: Russia has not implemented the 700 MHz digital dividend for mobile broadband. TV broadcasting and other services may continue to use spectrum above 694 MHz. This is a significant difference from EU countries which all cleared 694-790 MHz for MFCN.
verification_status: CONFIRMED — Russia has not cleared 700 MHz for mobile (DTT continues)

application: TDT (Televisión Digital Terrestre) — DVB-T with migration to DVB-T2 underway. 8 national multiplexes (RGE1, RGE2, MPE1-MPE5, MAUT) plus regional multiplexes. Channels 21-48 (8 MHz each). All broadcasts migrated to HD (MPEG-4) as of February 2024. Spain adopted new National Technical Plan for DVB-T2 with UHD in March 2025.
typical_devices: TDT-compatible receivers (Engel RT6130T2, Metronic DVB-T2 boxes), Samsung/LG/Sony TVs with DVB-T/T2 tuner, SPC Netzwerk DVB-T2 decoder
modulation: DVB-T: COFDM 64QAM (current); DVB-T2: COFDM 256QAM (rollout phase for UHD multiplex)
power_limit: High-power transmitters up to 20 kW ERP; medium-power 1-5 kW ERP; gap-filler network with low-power stations
regulatory_ref: Plan Técnico Nacional de la TDT (Royal Decree); MITECO (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica — manages spectrum); EU Decision 2017/899; ITU GE06 Agreement
notes: Spain completed 700 MHz clearance and refarming by 2020. All TDT now operates in 470-694 MHz. Spain completed HD migration (all channels in MPEG-4 H.264) in February 2024. A new National Technical Plan adopted in March 2025 introduces DVB-T2 for UHD, with one multiplex initially upgraded and phased rollout planned.

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors in TV white spaces
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Sennheiser EW-DX (Q1-9, R1-9, S1-10 bands), Audio-Technica 5000 Series
power_limit: 50 mW ERP (per ERC/REC 25-10 and Spanish national implementation)
regulatory_ref: CNAF (Cuadro Nacional de Atribución de Frecuencias); ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422; Secretaría de Estado de Telecomunicaciones
notes: Spain implements ERC/REC 25-10 through the CNAF. PMSE operates in TV white spaces on a secondary non-interference basis. Professional event production companies can coordinate with spectrum authorities for specific frequency assignments.

application: Audio PMSE in the 694-703 MHz lower guard band
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX, Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning ranges)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: CNAF; ECC/DEC/(15)01; EU Decision 2016/687
notes: Spain made the 694-703 MHz guard band available for PMSE following the 700 MHz clearance, consistent with the EU harmonised framework.

application: DVB-T2 HEVC digital terrestrial television — Italy completed switchover to DVB-T2 with HEVC (H.265) encoding by July 2022 (phased regionally from January 2022). Up to 12 national multiplexes planned by AGCOM. 40 Mbit/s per multiplex with DVB-T2 256QAM. Channels 21-48 (8 MHz each).
typical_devices: Decoder DVB-T2 HEVC Main 10 (mandatory standard for Italian market), Samsung/LG/Sony/Panasonic TVs with DVB-T2 HEVC tuner, I-Can/Telesystem/Digiquest DVB-T2 set-top boxes
modulation: COFDM DVB-T2: 256QAM, HEVC Main 10 profile video codec (H.265)
power_limit: High-power transmitters up to 50 kW ERP; medium and low-power relay sites throughout mountainous terrain
regulatory_ref: AGCOM (Autorità per le Garanzie nelle Comunicazioni) multiplex plan; MISE (Ministero dello Sviluppo Economico) frequency plan; EU Decision 2017/899; ITU GE06 Agreement; Legislative Decree 8 November 2021 n. 208
notes: Italy completed a complex DVB-T2 switchover in 2022, one of the largest in Europe. The country has challenging terrain (Alps, Apennines) requiring extensive relay networks. Italy has more DTT multiplexes than most EU countries due to high DTT platform reliance (over 90% of Italian households use DTT). Private broadcasters (Mediaset, La7) and public RAI all transitioned to DVB-T2 HEVC.

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors in TV white spaces
typical_devices: Shure Axient Digital (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Sennheiser EW-DX (Q1-9, R1-9, S1-10 bands), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (DG1: 470-700 MHz)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP (per ERC/REC 25-10 and Italian MISE regulations)
regulatory_ref: MISE frequency allocation; ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422; AGCOM regulations
notes: PMSE availability in Italy is more constrained than in some other EU countries due to the high number of DTT multiplexes occupying more channels. Fewer TV white space channels are typically available at any given location.

application: Audio PMSE in the 694-703 MHz lower guard band
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX, Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning ranges)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: MISE frequency plan; ECC/DEC/(15)01; EU Decision 2016/687
notes: Italy allocated the 694-703 MHz guard band for PMSE following the EU harmonised approach.

application: DTT was shut down in Switzerland in June 2019. SRG SSR (the Swiss public broadcaster) discontinued all over-the-air terrestrial TV transmission. The band remains allocated to broadcasting in the Swiss frequency plan but is not actively used for DTT.
typical_devices: N/A — no active DTT service. Swiss consumers use cable (UPC/Sunrise), IPTV (Swisscom Blue TV), satellite, or streaming.
power_limit: N/A (no active transmissions)
regulatory_ref: BAKOM (Bundesamt für Kommunikation / OFCOM Switzerland) National Frequency Allocation Plan 2022; ITU GE06 Agreement (Switzerland retains GE06 coordination rights)
notes: CRITICAL: Switzerland is UNIQUE in Europe — it shut down DTT in June 2019. SRG SSR decided the platform was not economically viable given <2% DTT household penetration. The 470-694 MHz band remains formally allocated to broadcasting in the Swiss frequency plan and under GE06, but no DTT transmitters are operational. This makes the band potentially available for other uses (PMSE, 5G Broadcast trials, etc.) on a national basis without causing DTT interference. Switzerland is not an EU member but follows CEPT framework.
verification_status: CONFIRMED — Switzerland (SRG SSR) shut down DTT terrestrial broadcasting June 2019

application: Wireless microphones and in-ear monitors — with no active DTT, the entire 470-694 MHz band is effectively available for PMSE in Switzerland (subject to cross-border coordination with neighbouring countries' DTT)
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX (full range Q1-9 through S7-10: 470.2-693.8 MHz), Shure Axient Digital (Band G56: 470-636 MHz), Audio-Technica 5000 Series (DG1: 470-700 MHz)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP (per BAKOM regulations and ERC/REC 25-10)
regulatory_ref: BAKOM frequency regulations; ERC/REC 25-10; ETSI EN 300 422; Swiss Radiocommunications Ordinance (FMG/VFR)
notes: With no active DTT, Switzerland offers uniquely favourable conditions for PMSE in the 470-694 MHz band. However, cross-border coordination with France, Germany, Italy, and Austria is still required under GE06 — PMSE near borders must avoid channels used by neighbouring countries' DTT transmitters.

application: Audio PMSE in the 694-703 MHz guard band
typical_devices: Sennheiser EW-DX, Shure Axient Digital (upper tuning ranges)
power_limit: 50 mW ERP
regulatory_ref: BAKOM frequency plan; ECC/DEC/(15)01
notes: Switzerland follows the CEPT harmonised approach for the 694-703 MHz guard band despite not being an EU member. With no DTT, this guard band is particularly useful for PMSE.

application: DVB-T/DVB-T2 — this is European UHF channel 38 (606-614 MHz in EU numbering). Used as a normal DTT channel in France. NOT allocated for WMTS (WMTS is US-only).
typical_devices: Standard DVB-T/T2 receivers (same as 470-694 MHz DTT)
power_limit: Same as general DTT allocation (up to 20 kW ERP at high-power sites)
regulatory_ref: ANFR frequency plan; ITU GE06 Agreement
notes: CORRECTION: 608-614 MHz is NOT WMTS in Europe. It is simply UHF channel 38 (EU) used for normal DTT broadcasting. The WMTS service (608-614 MHz / TV Channel 37) exists ONLY in the United States under FCC Part 95 Subpart H. In Europe, medical telemetry uses different bands (e.g., MBAN at 2360-2400 MHz, or ISM bands). [FACTCHECK NOTE: European DVB-T channel 38 is 606-614 MHz (8 MHz wide).
